Image 1 is the character sheet; draw Harry (the man on the far left: adult man of about thirty, messy dark-brown hair, light stubble, olive-green shirt with rolled sleeves, charcoal trousers, brown boots, worn brown satchel) exactly as shown. Ignore the other people on the sheet; they are not in this scene. Image 2 is the establishing picture of the alley where this scene happens: keep exactly this place (same crumbling stucco-and-brick walls, the same small arched, riveted, rusty iron sewer door low in the right-hand wall at ground level with grille slats and blackness behind, the bin, crate, bottles, drainpipe, and the bright sunny main avenue visible at the alley mouth), and match its painterly style and palette. Sunny afternoon outside, cool blue shadow inside the alley.

The Voice is never shown as a person: nobody is behind or in the door, no face, no hands, only blackness behind the slats and at most two tiny faint glints. Harry is the only person in the picture.

Moment: Harry, feeling down, has wandered into the alley; a chatty voice suddenly speaks and he realises it comes from the sewer door right at his feet. Framing: medium-wide shot along the alley. Harry stands right beside the low sewer door, mid-step, frozen, half turned and bending slightly, staring down at the door by his boots with wide eyes and raised eyebrows, one hand lifted in surprise. His posture is a little slumped and tired (he was feeling down). Two tiny glints in the dark behind the slats. Mood: eerie yet whimsical, a startled double-take. Keep Harry and the door in the right two-thirds; the left third is the dark shadowed wall, uncluttered.

Painterly storybook illustration matching the reference style: warm textured gouache and watercolour, soft grainy paper, hand-drawn ink lines. Landscape 4:3. No text, letters or signage anywhere.
